rows.input: the answer of a request: status and JSON body
rows.metadata: generation of the request for its resource (beginRequest, or openSource for the bootstrap), taken before it is sent; epoch and seq of X-Pixdcon-Position
rows.fence: ordering.js beginRequest and openSource before the request is sent; the caller hands the Answer to store.applyAnswer, which decides with decideView, decideAnswer or decideSnapshot; an answer without a readable header has epoch null and is not applied

rows.input: the last frame of one display as bytes (GET /api/v2/devices/<name>/preview)
rows.metadata: generation of the request for "frame:<device>", taken before it is sent; the page epoch and the incarnation of the device when it was sent
rows.fence: store.js decideFrameAnswer: it fills an empty slot only, for the newest request of that device, in the same epoch and life of the device; the stream's frames are never replaced by it

rows.input: the 20 s silence timer of the current stream

rows.input: every live event: snapshot, device, device-removed, preview, overlays, settings, scenes, config, mqtt, controller, log, ping

rows.fence: not handed on from a replaced stream or with an unreadable id or body; store.applyEvent: decideEvent first, then decideSnapshot, decideView or forgetDevice

resolved.store.applySnapshot: The body is synchronous and pure: it receives nothing asynchronous itself. It is the caller of the fence (decideSnapshot, then decideView for every view with snapshot: true); the sites that deliver to it have their own rows: live.js stream.addEventListener (the first event of a stream) and api.js fetch#1 (the bootstrap answer).
resolved.store.applyEvent: The body is synchronous and pure: it receives nothing asynchronous itself. It is the caller of the fence (decideEvent, then decideView, decideSnapshot or forgetDevice); the site that delivers to it has its own row: live.js stream.addEventListener.
resolved.store.applyAnswer: The body is synchronous and pure: it receives nothing asynchronous itself. It is the caller of the fence (decideView for a view, decideAnswer for a whole resource, decideSnapshot for the bootstrap); the site that delivers to it has its own row: api.js fetch#1.
